summary: Bayswater Lighthouse: a square wooden tower of 1913 beside Route 845 on the Saint John River, deactivated in 2005 and federally designated in 2018.

facts.agency: Bayswater Lighthouse Non Profit Group (owner since 2019); previously the Canadian Coast Guard

events.note: Built by B. R. Palmer of Tennant's Cove; contract price $825.
Two-year lease of the lighthouse to a community group.
Rotted beams found when the shingles were removed; demolition proposed, then stopped after community protest.
Designated a heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act.
Ownership to the Bayswater Lighthouse Non Profit Group.
Internal beams replaced and tower repainted with $80,000 in federal funds.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives 8.2 m (26.9 ft); the Lighthouse Directory gives 8 m (27 ft); Historic Places Days gives 8.8 m and also converts it to 26 feet (8.8 m is about 29 feet); the brief gives 8.8 m. The story gives each figure with its source.

LighthouseFriends (undated) says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the light; the Lighthouse Directory, revised 2026, says ownership passed to the Bayswater Lighthouse Non Profit Group in 2019. The story uses the 2019 transfer.

LighthouseFriends dates the rot discovery to October 2016 and names the Department of Fisheries and Oceans; the Lighthouse Directory says the Coast Guard found it in November 2016. The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends gives 1913; a Marine keepers' table gives an appointment date of 31 December 1913 for an F. E. Currie, but the station column is unreadable, so it is only consistent with the LighthouseFriends date.

LighthouseFriends attaches the $825 contract to Bayswater. The 1913-14 Marine report names B. R. Palmer of Tennant's Cove against a $825 contract in the block of tower works, but the OCR columns do not show which row that price belongs to, and the report's station column is not legible enough to match rows to Bayswater or McColgan Point.

notes_for_editor: Verified 2026-10-27 against LighthouseFriends (ID 1148), the 2018 Parks Canada release (news release, 4 June 2018), the Rowlett directory (nbs.htm), the Historic Places Days page, and the 1915 and 1916 Marine report volumes read through the corpus (identifiers 1915v50i16p21_1119 for the fiscal year 1913-14, and 1916v51i17p21_1196 for the keepers' table). Corrections made: the 1914 lens event was removed from the research record (the report's row is not matched to Bayswater); the story no longer says the report lists McColgan Point's sixth-order lens; the heights now give each source's figure (LighthouseFriends 8.2 m / 26.9 ft; Historic Places Days' 8.8 m is about 29 feet, not the 26 feet it also gives); the rot discovery is attributed to DFO (LighthouseFriends, October 2016) and to the Coast Guard (Lighthouse Directory, November 2016); the MP is named as the MP for Fundy Royal in the release; the keeper's table entry is stated as unconfirmed. Position-matched rows (not resolved): the 1913-14 report's New Brunswick block (scan p. 48-49) and the 1915-16 keepers' table (scan p. 73) are OCR columns. The Palmer $825 contract, the 27-foot tower with fourth-order lens, the fifth-order and sixth-order rows, and the F. E. Currie 31 December 1913 appointment cannot be matched to a station from the OCR; the page image could not be retrieved in this check (the archive.org image endpoints returned errors and the full scan archive is 229 MB), so the story states that the station column is not legible. A checker with image access should read scan pages 48, 49 and 73 before any row is attributed to Bayswater. Other open items: LighthouseFriends is undated and still gives the Canadian Coast Guard as owner (the Lighthouse Directory names the Non Profit Group since 2019); the Lighthouse Directory says the group had leased the lighthouse since 2012, while LighthouseFriends gives a two-year lease from 2010. Living people: none named beyond the MP and the 1913-1923 keeper F. E. Currie, whose service ended before 1960.
